definition: The strategy used to set the initial values of a neural network's parameters before training begins.
details: Good initialization (e.g., Xavier/Glorot or He initialization) helps gradients flow properly at the start of training and can significantly affect convergence speed and final performance.
story: Imagine teaching a friend to shoot a basketball. They miss, and you walk them backwards through the shot — elbow, wrist, release — to find what needs fixing. In plain words: The strategy used to set the initial values of a neural network's parameters before training begins. Here is how it actually plays out: Good initialization (e.g., Xavier/Glorot or He initialization) helps gradients flow properly at the start of training and can significantly affect convergence speed and final performance. It is learning from every miss instead of repeating the same mistake. That steady, miss-by-miss improvement is Weight Initialization.
